subject: Schedule reconciliation, rollback options and contingency checklist

Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: MAP timeline drift — need reconciliation and fallbacks

Hi Connor,

We're seeing slippage on milestones tied to our evaluation plan (security review finished later than expected, and the integration PoC is running into test-data sanitization work). Our expected close date (June 30) is at risk.

Can you share a reconciliation of the MAP vs. what Redwood needs from us to keep the current target? Specifically: what minimal items would allow us to keep the canary in prod without the final procurement milestone, and what are the realistic rollback/fallback options if we miss June 30?

I've attached the latest internal MAP spreadsheet and a brief risk summary. Procurement wants concrete contingency steps they can sign off on.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Ellis
Director of Platform Integrations, Cicero Health
(s) 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: MAP timeline drift — need reconciliation and fallbacks

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. I pulled the MAP and sketched a reconciliation runbook (high level) below.

Short answer: we can preserve a June 30 surface for a limited canary if Cicero agrees to a minimal acceptance gate and a documented rollback window. If the security/POC items slip beyond the buffer, we should rebaseline to a July 28 target and execute the rollback sequence to the previous stable model and route.

Proposed reconciliation checklist (minimal items to keep June 30 canary):
- Final tokenization & test-data whitelist applied to PoC (Cicero owners)
- Shared SOC-2 evidence packet delivered to your audit team (Redwood to supply subset)
- Feature-flagged canary with 2-hour rollback window and automated failover to predecessor model
- Acceptance criteria: 48h performance and quality sanity checks by Cicero with predefined pass thresholds

Rollback / contingency options (if above cannot be met):
A) Predecessor model fallback + traffic throttling (no new features)
B) Short-term extension (28 days) with formal canary postponement and credit for any SLA miss
C) Staggered rollout: initial internal-only canary for engineering + delayed external ramp

I'll attach the reconciliation spreadsheet and a brief runbook. Marissa and Laura — tagging you for pricing/credits and procurement coordination.

Connor
Connor O'Brien

Connor / Samantha — brief commercial note: if Cicero needs the July 28 extension option, we can offer a one-time bridging credit to cover the first two weeks of dedicated capacity, and we will honor the quoted price assuming the signed amendment arrives within 3 business days of the requested extension.

If the account needs an SLA credit for the missed June milestone, we'll need a short justification (impact to production) and an exec approval. I'll coordinate the approval path once you confirm the scenario.
